confidence_note: Verified in a full text of A New Earth (ch. 5 The Pain-Body, ch. 6 Breaking Free). Old text's invented examples (late arrival, sharp criticism), the claim 'the pain-body hates awareness' and the question 'is my pain-body waking up?' are dropped; the story uses Tolle's own marriage example. Tolle's pain-body is his own concept, not a scientific finding; the story presents it as his claim.
facts: Tolle holds that any negative emotion not fully faced and let go leaves a remnant of pain; remnants join into an energy field living in the cells of the body, 'an accumulation of old emotional pain', which he calls the pain-body.
It has a dormant and an active stage; dormant usually a few weeks, sometimes days or months, rarely years.
When ready to feed it 'can use the most insignificant event as a trigger, something somebody says or does, or even a thought'.
Alone, it feeds on your thoughts, which turn negative; with other people, 'preferably your partner or a close family member', it provokes them to feed on the drama.

'You don't just marry your wife or husband, you also marry her or his pain-body.' Not long after moving in together, a partner's voice may turn harsh, she accuses or shouts, most likely over a relatively trivial matter, or goes withdrawn; asked what is wrong she says 'Nothing', while her hostile energy says 'Everything is wrong'.
Tolle says the person who speaks then is the pain-body speaking through her, not the real face.

People with dense pain-bodies blow insignificant matters up out of all proportion; they cannot tell the difference between an event and their reaction to it. Road rage over someone driving too slowly is one of his examples.

Freedom begins with realising you have a pain-body and being present enough to notice it as a heavy influx of negative emotion when it becomes active; recognised, it can no longer pretend to be you and loses energy once the link to your thinking is cut.
scene_details: a partner's voice turning harsh over a trivial matter
'Nothing is wrong' said while the energy says 'Everything is wrong'
a driver in road rage over someone driving too slowly
the weeks of dormancy before it wakes
tension: A trivial remark meets a reaction out of all proportion, and Tolle says the size of the reaction belongs to something older.
opening_idea: Open on the couple moving in together and the sudden change of voice over something small, before Tolle's name for it.

lessons.idea: When a reaction is far bigger than its trigger, look for the older feeling before arguing about the trigger.
lessons.anchor: Tolle's 'Nothing is wrong' said with a hostile energy that says everything is.
lessons.example: Someone snaps at a friend over a late reply and, once calm, sees the snap was about something that had been building for weeks.

reflect_final: Think of your last reaction that was bigger than its trigger: what had been building before it, and what did you notice in your body at the start?

use_cases.situation: You feel a sudden heavy wave of irritation over something small.
use_cases.move: Notice it as a heavy influx of emotion in the body before replying, as Tolle suggests; wait one breath before you speak.

use_cases.situation: Your partner turns hostile over something trivial and says 'nothing is wrong'.
use_cases.move: Leave the trivial thing alone and ask softly later, when it has passed, what has been weighing on them.

use_cases.situation: A colleague overreacts in a meeting.
use_cases.move: Respond to the feeling instead of the content: 'This seems to matter a lot to you. Do you want to tell me more?'

pocket_idea: Tolle says a trivial trigger can wake old pain: notice the heavy wave before you answer it.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Tolle says you marry your partner's pain-body too, and it shows up over something trivial.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Tolle's pain-body: leftover emotion that goes dormant, wakes on a trivial trigger, and feeds on thoughts or on drama with a partner; noticing it as a heavy wave stops it passing for you.
